description: Fixed evaluation problems. Each debate is the prompt followed by three scripted user follow-ups, so older rounds can be condensed into a rolling summary.

problems.prompt: I'm a backend engineer at a large bank earning $165k with good benefits. A 12-person fintech startup offered me $140k plus 0.4% equity to be their second backend hire. Should I take it?
followUps: I have about 8 months of expenses saved and no dependents, but I'm planning to buy a condo in two years.
The startup raised a $6M seed round 10 months ago. They haven't told me their runway. What should I ask them before deciding?
Say they have 14 months of runway and won't budge on salary. Give me your final call and what would change it.

problems.prompt: My director wants me to move from senior engineer to engineering manager for my team of 6. I like coding but I'm curious about management. How should I decide?
followUps: The company says I could switch back to IC within a year if it doesn't work out, but nobody has actually done that here.
Two people on the team are senior to me in tenure, and one of them also wanted the role.
I have to answer by Friday. What exactly should I say to my director?

problems.prompt: I'm 27, working as a data analyst. Should I quit to do a full-time two-year master's in machine learning, which costs $70k, or keep working and learn on the side?
followUps: My employer offers $5k a year in tuition reimbursement for part-time programs, with a one-year stay commitment after each payment.
My goal is to be doing ML engineering work, not research, within three years.
One of you is overvaluing credentials and one is undervaluing them. Settle it: what's the plan for the next 12 months?

problems.prompt: Our Rails monolith serves 40k daily users and 8 engineers work in it. Deploys take 45 minutes and teams step on each other. Leadership wants to move to microservices. Is that the right fix?
followUps: About 70% of the deploy time is the test suite. Most merge conflicts are in the billing and notifications code.
We have no dedicated platform or SRE people. One engineer knows Kubernetes.
Leadership needs a one-quarter plan. What do we do in the next 90 days, in order?

problems.prompt: We're building an order-tracking service expected to hit 5k writes per second at peak. Should we use Postgres or DynamoDB?
followUps: Queries are mostly by order ID, but customer support needs to search by email, date range, and status.
The team knows Postgres well and has never run DynamoDB in production. We're already on AWS.
Peak is only during two sales events a year; normal load is about 300 writes per second. Does that change your answer?

problems.prompt: We have a web team that knows React and TypeScript. We need iOS and Android apps for a habit-tracking product. React Native, Flutter, or two native apps?
followUps: The app needs offline support, home-screen widgets, and HealthKit/Google Fit integration.
We can hire at most one more engineer this year.
Investors want the iOS app in four months. Which approach, and what do we cut to make it?

problems.prompt: For our B2B SaaS, should we build our own authentication or use a provider like Auth0 or Clerk?
followUps: Enterprise customers are starting to ask for SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning.
Auth0's quote for our expected 50k monthly active users is about $2,400/month. Our total infrastructure bill is $6k/month.
Our CTO worries about vendor lock-in above everything else. How do we address that concretely?

problems.prompt: I'm launching a paid newsletter about personal finance for nurses. I have 1,200 free subscribers. Plan the first 3 months of the paid launch.
followUps: I can spend about 10 hours a week on it while working full time as a nurse.
I was thinking $8/month. Some readers said they'd pay but I haven't tested it.
What are the two numbers I should watch each week, and what would make me stop or pivot?

problems.prompt: Plan a two-day offsite for a remote team of 14 people across 4 time zones, with a $20k budget. The goal is to reset after a rough reorg.
followUps: Three people have young kids and can't be away overnight more than once. Two people are very introverted.
My VP wants a full day of roadmap planning. The team wants time to just reconnect.
Give me the final agenda for both days, hour by hour.

problems.prompt: We need to move 2TB of customer data from a self-hosted MySQL to a managed cloud database with under 15 minutes of downtime. Plan the migration.
followUps: Writes come in 24/7 but drop to about 50 per second between 2 and 5 a.m.
We've never done a rehearsal migration and the legal team requires that no data be lost.
What is the rollback plan if we find problems an hour after cutover?

problems.prompt: I want to be conversational in Spanish within 9 months for a move to Mexico City. I'm a complete beginner. Make me a plan.
followUps: I can do 45 minutes on weekdays and 2 hours on weekends. I've failed with Duolingo twice because I got bored.
My budget for classes or tutors is about $150 a month.
How will I know at month 3 and month 6 whether I'm on track?

problems.prompt: My 2012 Honda Civic has 160k miles and needs a $2,800 transmission repair. Should I fix it or buy another car?
followUps: Otherwise it runs fine. I drive about 9k miles a year, mostly commuting 15 miles each way.
I have $12k saved, and a used 2019 Civic around me costs about $19k.
My partner thinks we should get an EV now. Is that a good idea or a distraction?

problems.prompt: My roommate keeps having their partner stay over 4-5 nights a week. The partner doesn't pay rent and uses utilities. How should I handle it?
followUps: We're on a joint lease that ends in 7 months. I otherwise like my roommate.
I brought it up once casually and they said 'they're barely here' and changed the subject.
Write out what I should actually say, and what I'll do if they don't agree.

problems.prompt: My best friend's destination wedding in Portugal would cost me about $3,500 all in. I'm trying to pay off $9k of credit card debt. Should I go?
followUps: I'm a bridesmaid. She said she'd understand if I can't come, but I think she'd be hurt.
The card's interest rate is 24%. I pay about $600 a month toward it.
If I go, how do I do it as cheaply as possible? If I don't, how do I tell her?

problems.prompt: We're thinking of adopting a dog. We both work hybrid, three days in the office, in a one-bedroom apartment. Is now the right time?
followUps: There's a dog daycare nearby for $45 a day. Our building allows dogs under 40 pounds.
We might move to a bigger place or another city in about a year, but it's not certain.
If we go ahead, what kind of dog and what should the first month look like?
